title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction, compaction and spillover improvements to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation:
Current KV cache memory management suffers from fragmentation under mixed-length sequences and bursty workloads. In high-utilization scenarios we observed increased paging and occasional OOMs due to inability to compact or spill efficiently. This PR implements an adaptive eviction + compaction + spillover pipeline intended to: 1) reduce in-GPU fragmentation via lightweight on-the-fly compaction heuristics, 2) introduce adaptive paging thresholds that differentiate cold vs hot kv entries, and 3) implement a low-latency spillover path to host memory with asynchronous reclamation to avoid blocking inference.

What changed (high-level):
- New Eviction Manager that combines segmented-LRU (for recency) with size-aware priority to avoid evicting a small number of very large KV entries that cause fragmentation.
- Adaptive paging thresholds computed from rolling percentiles of live KV sizes + sequence length distribution; thresholds tuned per-device-type.
- In-GPU compaction pass: a background cooperative defragmenter that coalesces free regions when fragmentation crosses a configurable threshold. Compaction is throttled by SLO-aware token-rate budget.
- Spillover path: async spill-to-host using pinned staging buffers + a streaming worker pool; entries flagged as "spillable" are evicted from GPU and reconstructed on demand with a fast rehydrate path.
- Metrics + telemetry: added fragmentation_ratio, compaction_runs, spill_count, async_rehydrate_latency, eviction_score_histogram. These are exposed to the console and used in autopolicy heuristics.
- Configuration: added runtime knobs with safe defaults; documented in runtime/config/kv_cache.md.

Why this approach:
- Pure LRU was causing pathological evictions of many small entries while a few large entries caused fragmentation. The segmented-LRU + size-aware heuristics balance recency with fragmentation pressure.
- Eager compaction can harm latency; making compaction cooperative and SLO-aware prevents regressions.
- Spillover rather than immediate disk paging keeps critical hot state in GPU while moving cold, large, rarely used KV entries to host memory to avoid OOMs.

Benchmarks / results (internal perf lab):
- Under a mixed-length conversational workload (seq len 64/512/2048 distribution), tail OOMs reduced from 12 events/hour to 0 events/hour on the stress rig.
- Average token latency change: +0.8% (within noise).
- 95th percentile token latency decreased by 6% due to fewer forced synchronous evictions.
- GPU memory utilization smoother: fragmentation_ratio dropped from median 0.42 -> 0.18.
- Cost impact: spillover increases host memory usage ~120MB per-worker on heavy workloads but prevents expensive retries and instance restarts.

commits:
Initial implementation of eviction manager and interfaces
- skeleton for compactor and spillover worker
Adaptive threshold calculation and per-device tuning
Implement async spillover path with staged pinned buffers
Integrate compactor with kv_cache_manager and add SLO throttle
Add metrics, tests, docs and benchmark harness
Address review feedback: make thresholds observable and add unit-tests for rehydrate path
review_comments: Miguel Ortega: The segmented-LRU idea looks good, but can you add more detail on eviction_score computation and ensure it's deterministic across threads? Also request unit tests for concurrency edge cases.
Aisha Khan (author): Added deterministic tie-breaker based on allocation timestamp and added tests for concurrent eviction in tests/kv_cache/eviction_policy_test.cc.
Priya Raman: Compaction looks heavy — how do we ensure it doesn't steal cycles from inference? Please add SLO-aware throttling and a rate limiter.
Aisha Khan: Compactor now checks the token budget runway and uses cooperative yields; included integration test to assert no regression in tail latency.
Liam O'Connor: Spillover to host is necessary but watch for NUMA effects on multi-socket hosts. Add a fallback to local ephemeral SSD if host memory poorly performing.
Aisha Khan: Added NUMA-aware placement using the host allocator and documented the SSD fallback as a configurable option. Recorded a note in runtime/config/kv_cache.md.
CI (kv_cache pipeline): initial run failed on compaction integration test (flaky timing). Reran with extended timeouts and it passed.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction, background compaction, and async spillover to host memory to reduce fragmentation and OOMs. Added metrics and runtime knobs.
notes_for_ops: Deploy notes: enable adaptive spillover in heavy-usage clusters via runtime flag kv_cache.spillover.enabled=true. Monitor metrics kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio and kv_cache.spill_count; default thresholds are conservative. Rolling restart not required but recommended for nodes running pre-1.3.0 agents.
